summary: Adds a reusable skill for generating multi-sheet Excel workbooks with openpyxl, addressing common pitfalls like the default sheet artifact, formula string prefix handling, and cross-sheet reference syntax. Includes a verification helper script.

Updated excel-workbook-generation skill to address verifier/test mismatch seen in trace. Added test-driven generation workflow, explicit anti-patterns around self-verification traps, and reinforced use of the provided verify_workbook.py script. Added troubleshooting for exact string/format mismatches that commonly cause hidden test failures.

Updated excel-workbook-generation/SKILL.md to address common openpyxl pitfalls observed in the trace: ws.cell() requires integer indices for row/column (not letters), and variable names like 'row' shadow worksheet methods causing TypeErrors. Added explicit data preprocessing step (filtering/sorting) before writing to sheets.

Updated excel-workbook-generation/SKILL.md to enforce reading verifier/test expectations before coding, explicitly warn against inline verifiers, and clarify openpyxl anti-patterns observed in the trace (column letter TypeError, formula spacing, number format mismatches). Added targeted troubleshooting for test_legacy_pytest_suite failures.

Updated excel-workbook-generation skill to enforce mandatory test-first workflow, add multi-source data merging patterns (JSON+CSV+JSON), strengthen verification discipline, and add explicit decision rules that prevent the brittle inline-script approach seen in the failed trace.

Updated excel-workbook-generation skill to address trace failures: emphasized reading test_output.py before coding, added template update workflow (clearing stale rows), reinforced running official test suites over ad-hoc checks, and added anti-patterns for skipping verifiers and leaving stale template data.

The agent failed the official test suite despite passing 38/38 self-validation checks. The trace reveals two critical gaps in the existing excel-workbook-generation skill: (1) CSV column-to-field mapping pitfalls where agents assume column names match expected fields without verifying alignment, and (2) over-reliance on ad-hoc self-validation instead of running the official test suite early. This patch adds explicit CSV mapping verification steps, a decision rule to run official tests before self-validation, and a reusable CSV inspection helper script.

Updated excel-workbook-generation/SKILL.md to explicitly handle bridge/reconciliation CSVs with action columns (override/insert/delete), reinforce running the official test suite before submission, and add decision rules for when ad-hoc checks pass but tests fail.

The agent failed test_legacy_node_checks despite generating a workbook that appeared correct in inline verification. The trace reveals three critical gaps: (1) the agent skipped reading test_output.py before writing code, (2) relied on inline verification instead of running the official test suite first, and (3) dismissed a floating-point precision mismatch (5.8e-11) that likely caused the test failure. The existing excel-workbook-generation skill already covers most of this, but needs stronger enforcement of the test-first workflow, explicit guidance on floating-point comparisons in financial data, and a clearer troubleshooting path for legacy test failures.
